solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Planted one's plant OK

parts.note: planted oneself, i.e. sat down, gives SAT
one is, written I'S, gives IS
a plant is an industrial works or factory

explanation.surface: Someone who planted a plant pronounces it fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' repeated tempts a gardening reading; the second one is a manufacturing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean acceptable or good enough, an informal synonym pair.

clue.text: Fantastic character turning round our sphere?

indicators.note: the words are spun about, so their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A fantastical hero spinning our globe around, as in a comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning round' rearranges the letters of OUR SPHERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A caped crusader with powers is a fictional figure from fantasy comics.

clue.text: Demands to support Tory leader's charges

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits underneath and so holds up the first
the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: demands, as a verb, means asks

explanation.surface: Demands made to back up the Conservative leader's accusations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader's' takes T from Tory; 'to support' puts ASKS below it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Charges as duties or jobs entrusted to someone are assignments.

clue.text: Painting of dry French commmanding officer

parts.note: sec is the French word for dry
CO is the standard abbreviation for commanding officer (the clue prints the word with a triple m)

explanation.surface: A dry painting belonging to a French commanding officer.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as printed has a typo, 'commmanding', which does not affect the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: Secco is a technique of mural painting on dry plaster, as opposed to fresco.

clue.text: A salute keeping soldiers in conformity

indicators.note: one word keeps another, holding it inside

parts.note: to salute someone is to greet them
men is the usual crossword word for soldiers or rank-and-file troops

explanation.surface: A salute with soldiers lined up in uniform conformity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salute' as a verb tempts a military gesture, but it means hail someone; 'keeping' signals the soldiers held within.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in accord or harmony with others is a state of concord.

clue.text: Time went slow catching second shift

indicators.note: the outer letters catch and hold the inner one

parts.note: went, as in ran, moved quickly
a slow clock or train runs late

explanation.surface: Time dragged as someone caught the second shift at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' reads as a work shift but is the verb; 'catching' holds the second inside the run of time, went and slow.
explanation.definitionFit: To translate can mean to move or transfer from one place to another, as with a bishop or a body in physics.

clue.text: Regretted admitting Left governed

indicators.note: letting someone in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: rued means regretted

explanation.surface: Someone sorry for letting in the Left that governed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' places L inside RUED.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler holds sway, so a country that was governed was under a monarch's sway.

clue.text: Eager to see thin, sauciest pants

indicators.note: pants, British slang for rubbish, here signals the letters as a poor jumble to rearrange

explanation.surface: Keen to see thin, cheeky underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' (British slang for nonsense) rearranges THIN SAUCIEST; the surface treats it as underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone keen and full of zeal is enthusiastic, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Scruffs sleep best without cover

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

indicators.note: a word stripped of its covering loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: Scruffy types sleep best without a blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without cover' strips B and T from best, leaving ES.
explanation.definitionFit: The scruff of the neck is the back of it, the plural being the back-neck parts.

clue.text: Dogged mongrel's first to get docked

indicators.note: the mongrel's word is placed at the front of the answer

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
to dog someone is to follow or tail them

explanation.surface: A stubborn mongrel is the first to have its tail cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogged' looks like an adjective meaning stubborn but is the verb tailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Docking a tail or wages cuts them short, the same as cutting back.

clue.text: Pansies don't flourish outside current allotment

indicators.note: the rearranged letters lie outside the current symbol, enclosing it
to flourish a thing is to wave it about, so these letters are waved into a new order

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Pansies fail to thrive outside an allotment plot with current flowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flourish' rearranges PANSIES DONT; 'outside' places that around I, the physics symbol for current.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispensation is a distribution or apportioning of things, as is an allotment.

clue.text: Epoch or so possibly to create stars

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: An epoch or so may be needed to create stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges EPOCH OR SO; 'stars' looks astronomical but means the newspaper astrology column.
explanation.definitionFit: Your stars, in the informal sense, are an astrological forecast printed in the paper.

clue.text: Angles for fish on board ship

indicators.note: a thing on board a ship is inside it

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the usual abbreviation for a ship
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone angling for fish while on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angles' wants to be fishing, matching 'fish'; it means viewpoints. 'on board' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Different angles on an argument are its aspects or points of view.

clue.text: Place set out around clubs for performance

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the club symbol
out signals the letters as disordered and needing rearrangement

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A place setting laid out with clubs, for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PLACE SET and 'around' wraps that round C.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a show or display put on for an audience.

clue.text: Bland mousse? Let's attempt to eat it up

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the letters are read from the bottom
the words eat the answer, holding it inside them

explanation.surface: A bland mousse: let's have a go at eating it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat it' shows the answer is held in MOUSSE LETS AT, and 'up' reads that run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking flavour is the plain meaning of both words, a simple synonym.

clue.text: Fickle person's home with clean guttering

definitions.note: the 's is just 'is' linking definition and wordplay

indicators.note: a guttering candle flickers unsteadily, so the letters waver into a new order

explanation.surface: A fickle person's house with its gutters cleaned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guttering' rearranges HOME CLEAN; the surface reads it as roof guttering.
explanation.definitionFit: The lizard that changes colour gives its name to an inconstant person who changes opinions.

clue.text: Home, a chap's castle ultimately

parts.note: bod is slang for a chap or person

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter

explanation.surface: Home, as the saying goes, is a man's castle.
explanation.walkthrough: BOD is British slang for a person; 'ultimately' takes E from castle.
explanation.definitionFit: An abode is a dwelling, the place where one lives.

clue.text: Dirtiest old boy's oddly clean bedsit

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil, with the 's giving S

indicators.note: oddly takes the letters in odd positions

explanation.surface: An old boy's bedsit, oddly clean, though he is filthiest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes C, E, N, E, S, T from CLEAN BEDSIT. An old boy (OB) is a former pupil of a British school.
explanation.definitionFit: Most indecent or filthy, as in dirty jokes, is the superlative of obscene.

clue.text: Swears a volume with expressions of pain

parts.note: ow is a cry of pain, made plural

explanation.surface: Someone cursing with a whole book's worth of yelps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swears' suggests cursing; here it means declares solemnly.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to declare or assert openly, as one swears a fact.

clue.text: Performers about flipped before 'Hair'

indicators.note: the first piece comes ahead of the hair word
flipped means turned over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: CA, circa, is the Latin abbreviation for about
tresses are long locks of hair

explanation.surface: Performers who flipped before appearing in the musical Hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped' turns CA (circa) to AC. Hair is also a famous rock musical, which feeds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Actresses are female stage and screen performers.

clue.text: Handle the continental bird to start

indicators.note: the bird is placed at the start of the answer

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Grab the European bird to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' looks like a verb; it is a noun, a name or title.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is informal for a name, and a title is a name too.

clue.text: The Conservatives possibly including 'one of them'

indicators.note: one piece includes the other within it

parts.note: the right is a name for conservatives, abbreviated R
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The Tories possibly count someone as one of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts I inside THE + R, R being the right as in the political Right.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun means belonging to them, rendered by the phrase given.

clue.text: Outgoing former husband sober embracing pet?

parts.note: an ex is a former husband

indicators.note: the outer letters hug the inner piece

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking
Rover is a stock name for a pet dog

explanation.surface: A sociable ex-husband, now off drink, cuddling the pet.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the dog's name is only one example of a pet; 'embracing' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing, sociable person is the opposite of an introvert.

clue.text: All players show disapproving expression by half-time

parts.note: tut is a sound of disapproval

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: The whole squad tuts in disapproval at half-time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes TI from time. 'All players' sounds like a sports team; it is the musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is a direction in music for the whole orchestra to play together.

clue.text: Love died in fiction of classic film perhaps

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

indicators.note: one letter is placed in the word for fiction

parts.note: a fiction is an untruth, a lie
D is the abbreviation for died, used in dates

explanation.surface: In a classic film, love died in the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts D inside LIE, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is something old and popular, such as a golden-age movie or song.

clue.text: Extremely cerebral peak of superlative brilliance

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: Everest is the highest mountain peak

explanation.surface: The most cerebral peak of exceptional brilliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes C and L, the ends of cerebral.
explanation.definitionFit: Brightest and most intelligent, the top degree of cleverness.

clue.text: Maradona, say, with pass after pass

indicators.note: the first pass word comes after the second one

parts.note: to pass away is to die
to have a go is to take a turn, or a pass at something

explanation.surface: Maradona dribbling, a pass followed by another pass.
explanation.walkthrough: Diego Maradona was the Argentinian footballer; 'say' shows he is one example of a Diego.
explanation.definitionFit: Maradona's first name was this, so he is an example of someone bearing it.

clue.text: Feeling quietly hurt taking in Independent

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quietly

indicators.note: one word takes another into itself

parts.note: resentment is hurt or bitterness at being wronged

explanation.surface: Feeling quietly hurt at taking in the Independent newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' puts I inside RESENTMENT; The Independent is a British newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A presentiment is a feeling or foreboding that something will happen.
